heard: No nation can ever on the moon. During the intense geopolitical tensions of the Cold War, the United States and the Soviet Union faced a dangerous new frontier. On January 27, 1967, rival superpowers opened the Outer Space Treaty for signature in Washington, London, and Moscow. This foundational agreement strictly bans countries from placing nuclear weapons or weapons of mass destruction in Earth orbit. The treaty explicitly forbids claiming sovereignty over any celestial body and legally designates outer space as the province of all mankind. Yet remarkably, the treaty does not explicitly ban conventional military weapons in space. This Cold War relic keeps the heavens peaceful because no nation can ever own the moon.
